newsitem.title: USA: USWC heavy crudes seen weak, drying up ANS market.
newsitem.headline: USWC heavy crudes seen weak, drying up ANS market.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes rose with a stronger West Texas Intermediate (WTI) benchmark, traders said Wednesday, making the grades less attractive than heavy oils, which have fallen in price.
With most light crude trades done for February, traders said ample supplies of heavy grade are putting pressure on the March Alaska North Slope (ANS) market.
"Heavy is looking weaker. Postings are falling and there's a discount to postings," a trader said.
Traders said Tosco turned away delivery of February heavies Monday following a fire at its Calif. plant.
With heavy crude prices expected to drop below their current $17.40 range, refiners were looking at ways to run heavies instead of light grades.
Traders reported discounts held Wednesday at 50 to 25 cents under postings. Texaco on Tuesday lowered their posted prices 50 cents.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were offered at $17.55 and bid about $17.30.
Meanwhile, forecasts of cooler weather and tensions in Iraq lifted WTI crudes 60 cents in line with higher heating oil market.
Outright ANS prices rose equal amount, with a lack of bids holding the ANS differential at $1.45 under March WTI.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with not buyers stepped forward in early trade.
A major refinery bid $2.00 under March WTI.
